title: LLM Fine-tuning
oneLiner: Fine-tuning gives a general model extra, targeted practice so it follows instructions or masters a task; clever tricks like LoRA do it by training a tiny add-on instead of the whole model.

what.html:
A pre-trained model has read a lot but doesn't know your job. Fine-tuning trains it a bit more on examples of what you want: question–answer pairs (SFT), many kinds of instructions (instruction tuning), or a specialised domain. Updating every weight is expensive, so parameter-efficient methods train only small add-ons: learned prompt vectors, LoRA matrices, or adapters.

Everyday versionA new doctor finishing general training (pre-training) then doing a residency in cardiology (fine-tuning). LoRA is like giving them a slim specialist handbook rather than rewriting everything they learned.

why.html:
• Chat assistants are fine-tuned base models.
  • LoRA and QLoRA let you fine-tune large models on one GPU.
  • Careless fine-tuning can make a model forget other skills.

how.title: Why and when
how.html: Fine-tune for consistent format, style, a specialised task or a cheaper model. For new facts, retrieval usually works better.

how.title: Learn from example answers
how.html: SFT shows the model prompts with ideal answers. Only the answer words count toward the loss, so it learns to answer, not to copy questions.

how.title: Many tasks as instructions
how.html: Train on hundreds of task types, each written as an instruction. The model learns to follow instructions it has never seen.

how.title: Learn a few steering vectors
how.html: Keep the model frozen and learn a short set of special input vectors (prompt tuning) or extra keys/values at every layer (prefix tuning).

how.title: LoRA: a thin correction
how.html: Add two thin matrices whose product nudges a big weight matrix. Rank 8 on a 1000 × 1000 matrix trains just 16,000 numbers, 1.6%.

how.title: QLoRA and adapters
how.html: Store the frozen model in 4-bit and train LoRA on top: a 7B model drops from about 112 GB to under 4 GB. Adapters add small extra layers instead.

how.title: Merge and distil
how.html: Add together the changes from different fine-tunes to combine skills, or train a small student to copy a big teacher's answers and probabilities.

how.title: Don't forget the old skills
how.html: Training only on new data can erase old abilities. Mix in some old data, train fewer weights, and test widely.

demo.html: Match each description to the fine-tuning method.

example.html:
LoRA arithmetic. Matrix 1000 × 1000 = 1,000,000 weights. Rank 8: B is 1000 × 8 and A is 8 × 1000, so 8,000 + 8,000 = 16,000 trainable numbers, 1.6% of the original.

Supplementary Because B starts at zero, the fine-tuned model begins exactly where the base model was; after training, B × A can be folded into the original weights so answers are no slower.

misunderstandings: Fine-tuning is the best way to teach new facts.
Retrieval usually is; fine-tuning changes behaviour.
More fine-tuning data is always better.
It can also erase old ones.
takeaways: Fine-tune for behaviour: format, task, domain, style.
SFT trains on responses only; instruction tuning generalises across tasks.
Prompt/prefix tuning learn input or per-layer vectors.
LoRA: r(d + k) parameters (1.6% at r = 8 on 1000²); QLoRA uses a 4-bit base.
Merging adds task vectors; distillation copies a teacher; watch for forgetting.
thirty: Fine-tuning specialises a pre-trained model. Full fine-tuning updates all weights (≈16 B/param with Adam). SFT trains on prompt–response pairs with the loss masked to the response; instruction tuning does SFT over many task types so the model follows unseen instructions. PEFT freezes the base: prompt tuning learns n input embeddings, prefix tuning learns per-layer keys/values, adapters insert bottleneck layers, and LoRA learns ΔW = BA with rank r (r(d + k) parameters: 16,000 = 1.6% for r = 8 on 1000 × 1000), B initialised to zero and mergeable for zero latency. QLoRA keeps the base in 4-bit NF4 (7B: ≈3.6 GB vs 112 GB for full fine-tuning). Merging adds task vectors (fine-tuned − base); distillation trains a student on a teacher's soft outputs at temperature T. Catastrophic forgetting overwrites old skills; mitigate with replay, PEFT, regularisation and broad evaluation.
